# EggEncoder — Full Reference

> Audio encoding/decoding toolkit for .NET — 12 formats (AAC, AIFF incl. AIFC, ALAC, AU, FLAC, MP3, Opus, TTA, Vorbis, WAV incl. IMA/MS/Yamaha ADPCM and G.711, WavPack, WMA) plus MOV/MP4 probing, mostly pure C# alongside native MP3/FLAC/WavPack P/Invoke bindings, built-in waveform/peak/RMS generation, and an opt-in PCM transform pipeline (resampling, gain/peak normalization, dynamics compression, noise gating, peak limiting, pan/balance, channel remix, bit-depth/float conversion, fades, parametric EQ, FIR filtering, mixing, concatenation), behind one IMediaEncoder interface.

## Overview

EggEncoder gives you a single `IMediaEncoder` abstraction for probing, converting, and cutting audio files, implemented entirely in-process by `NativeEncoder`: mostly pure .NET codec implementations (AAC, AIFF/AIFC, ALAC, AU, TTA, Opus, Vorbis, WAV incl. all its ADPCM/G.711 variants, WMA) plus native P/Invoke bindings to `libmp3lame`, `libFLAC`, and `wavpackdll` for MP3, FLAC, and WavPack specifically. No external process, no ffmpeg install, no subprocess overhead. The native-binary-backed codecs (MP3, FLAC, WavPack) are Windows x64 only; the pure-managed codecs have no such restriction, but this library as a whole ships and is tested as a Windows x64 package.

## Installation

```bash
dotnet add package EggEncoder
```

Targets `net8.0`, `net9.0`, `net10.0`. Native codec binaries (`libmp3lame.dll`, `libFLAC.dll`, `wavpackdll.dll`) for `win-x64` ship inside the package via the NuGet `contentFiles` convention and are copied to your output directory at `Native/win-x64/*.dll` automatically — no separate install step.

## Core Interface

```csharp
namespace EggEncoder;

public interface IMediaEncoder
{
    Task<ProbeResult> Probe(string filePath);
    Task ConvertFile(string sourceFilePath, string destFilePath);
    Task CutFile(string sourceFilePath, string destFilePath, int startInSeconds, int endInSeconds);
}
```

```csharp
public class ProbeResult
{
    public string FormatName { get; init; }        // e.g. "wav", "flac", "mp3", "aac", "asf", "mov", "mp4"
    public string FormatLongName { get; init; }     // e.g. "WAV / WAVE (Waveform Audio)"
    public long SizeBytes { get; init; }
    public double DurationSeconds { get; init; }
    public string CodecType { get; init; }          // "audio" or "video"
    public string? CodecName { get; init; }         // e.g. "pcm_s16le", "adpcm_yamaha", "flac", "mp3", "aac", "wmav2"
    public string? CodecLongName { get; init; }
    public int? SampleRate { get; init; }
    public int? Channels { get; init; }
    public string? ChannelLayout { get; init; }     // "mono", "stereo", or "{n} channels"
    public int? BitsPerSample { get; init; }
    public int? BitRate { get; init; }
    public bool? IsVariableBitRate { get; init; }   // MP3 only
    public long? DurationInSamples { get; init; }
    public string? TimeBase { get; init; }          // e.g. "1/44100"
    public int? Width { get; init; }                // set for video containers (MOV/MP4), null for audio
    public int? Height { get; init; }
    public IReadOnlyList<double>? Waveform { get; init; }  // normalized peak windows in [0,1], or null
    public double? PeakAmplitude { get; init; }     // loudest absolute sample across the whole decode, normalized to [0,1]
    public double? RmsLevel { get; init; }          // root-mean-square level across every sample, normalized to [0,1] (not ITU-R BS.1770 loudness)
}
```

Only fields this library can genuinely compute are populated -- nothing is filled with ffprobe-style placeholders (e.g. no `probe_score`, no disposition flags). `PeakAmplitude`/`RmsLevel` are null wherever `Waveform` is null (e.g. a MOV/MP4 file with no decodable audio track).

## Dependency Injection

```csharp
using EggEncoder;

builder.Services.AddEggEncoder(); // registers IMediaEncoder -> NativeEncoder (scoped)
// optional: AddEggEncoder(enableLogging: false) to silence Start/Completed/Failed logging entirely
```

`AddEggEncoder` also maps `IPcmTransformEncoder` (the PCM transform pipeline's own DI-friendly entry point — see "PCM Transform Pipeline" below) to resolve that same scoped `NativeEncoder` instance; inject whichever interface fits the call site.

### Consuming IMediaEncoder

```csharp
public class MediaService(IMediaEncoder mediaEncoder)
{
    public Task<ProbeResult> Inspect(string filePath) => mediaEncoder.Probe(filePath);
    public Task Transcode(string sourcePath, string destPath) => mediaEncoder.ConvertFile(sourcePath, destPath);
    public Task Trim(string sourcePath, string destPath, int startSeconds, int endSeconds) =>
        mediaEncoder.CutFile(sourcePath, destPath, startSeconds, endSeconds);
}
```

### Without DI

```csharp
using EggEncoder;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions;

IMediaEncoder encoder = new NativeEncoder(NullLogger<NativeEncoder>.Instance);
var probeResult = await encoder.Probe("track.flac");
```

### From a background worker (no request-scoped DI)

```csharp
public class TranscodeWorker(IServiceProvider serviceProvider)
{
    public async Task RunAsync(string sourcePath, string destPath)
    {
        await using var scope = serviceProvider.CreateAsyncScope();
        var mediaEncoder = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<IMediaEncoder>();
        await mediaEncoder.ConvertFile(sourcePath, destPath);
    }
}
```

## Supported Formats

| Format | Probe | Decode | Encode |
|--------|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| WAV    | yes | yes | yes |
| AIFF / AIFC | yes | yes | yes |
| AU (.au) | yes | yes | yes |
| ALAC (.caf) | yes | yes | yes |
| TTA    | yes | yes | yes |
| WavPack (.wv) | yes | yes | yes |
| Opus (.opus) | yes | yes | yes |
| Vorbis (.ogg) | yes | yes | yes |
| FLAC   | yes | yes | yes |
| MP3    | yes | yes | yes |
| AAC    | yes | yes | yes |
| WMA    | yes | yes | yes |
| MOV/MP4 | yes | yes¹ | no |

¹ MOV/MP4 decode is audio-only (mono AAC-LC tracks); video frames are never decoded. Files without a matching audio track still probe fine (metadata only) -- `NativeEncoder.Probe` falls back gracefully rather than failing the whole probe.

`AudioCutter.Cut` (used by `NativeEncoder.CutFile`) decodes any supported source format and writes to any supported destination format -- it can transcode while trimming; source and destination extensions no longer need to match. Sample-accurate, no re-encode of the untouched region.

### WAV's own format-tag variants

WAV supports 8-bit unsigned, 16/24/32-bit signed integer, and 32-bit IEEE float PCM, both read and write (`WavSampleFormat.Integer`/`Float32`). Beyond plain PCM, `WavReader`/`WavWriter` also cover, all picked up automatically from the file's own `fmt` chunk on read (no opt-in needed) and selectable as a `WavSampleFormat` destination on write:

- **IMA ADPCM** (format tag 17) -- mono/stereo only, reports/requires 16-bit PCM at the boundary regardless of the 4-bit coded width. Block-structured: `WavWriter` buffers samples internally into fixed-size blocks (1024-byte block align, matching FFmpeg's own real `adpcm_ima_wav` encoder default) and only physically writes once a block fills or `Finish()` is called, which also flushes and pads any final short block. Each nibble is chosen by an 8-candidate brute-force search (`ImaAdpcmDecoder.QuantizeNibble`) against the same per-bit-term diff formula `ExpandNibble` itself decodes with -- confirmed, not assumed, that FFmpeg's own real encoder's nibble-picking heuristic optimizes for a formula that genuinely disagrees with its own decoder's, so a search (not a closed-form computation) is what keeps this encoder's running state in lockstep with any standards-compliant decoder.
- **MS ADPCM** (format tag 2) -- mono/stereo only, same 16-bit-boundary/4-bit-coded-width story. A genuinely different algorithm from IMA ADPCM: linear prediction via a per-file coefficient table carried in the `fmt` chunk extension itself, not IMA ADPCM's universal fixed step table -- its own decoder/encoder (`MsAdpcmDecoder`/`MsAdpcmEncoder`), not a variant of the IMA ADPCM types. Unlike IMA ADPCM, the nibble is computed via a direct closed-form formula (confirmed FFmpeg's own real encoder's internal state-tracking formula structurally matches its own decoder's, so no search is needed); the encoder always selects the standard coefficient table's simplest pair for every block, matching FFmpeg's own real encoder exactly.
- **Yamaha ADPCM** (format tag 32) -- mono/stereo only, same 16-bit-boundary/4-bit-coded-width story. Structurally simpler than IMA/MS ADPCM: confirmed directly from FFmpeg's real source and a real ffmpeg-produced fixture's own bytes, it has **no block structure at all** -- no per-block header, no `wSamplesPerBlock` `fmt` chunk extension (`cbSize` is 0) -- each channel's predictor/step state just carries continuously for the whole stream, lazily initializing only the first time a channel's own step is still its default 0. Like MS ADPCM, the nibble is a direct closed-form formula, not a search. Because there's no block padding, the data chunk size is exactly `ceil(totalFrames * channels / 2)` bytes, with at most one trailing zero-pad nibble (mono, odd frame count) flushed by `Finish()`.
- **G.711 mu-law/A-law** (format tags 7/6) -- any channel count (no mono/stereo restriction, unlike every ADPCM variant above), reports/requires 16-bit PCM at the boundary regardless of the 8-bit coded width. No block structure or adaptive state at all, so encode is a simple one-sample-at-a-time companding formula, selected via `WavSampleFormat.MuLaw`/`ALaw` the same way `Float32` is.

All three ADPCM variants and G.711 are verified bit-exact against a real, independent ffmpeg decode of files this library's own encoders produced. Samples are always exchanged as `int[]`, at this codebase's native-range convention for whatever bit depth is in play (see "PCM Transform Pipeline" below).

## PCM Transform Pipeline

A `PcmTransformPipeline` runs a list of `IPcmTransform`s over every decoded block between decode and the destination write. It's opt-in -- the plain `Convert`/`Cut` above are untouched and still fully streaming.

```csharp
using EggEncoder.Codecs;
using EggEncoder.Pcm;

var pipeline = new PcmTransformPipeline(
    new ResamplingTransform(sourceRate: 44100, targetRate: 48000, channels: 2),
    new CompressorTransform(sampleRate: 48000, thresholdDb: -18, ratio: 4, attackMs: 10, releaseMs: 150),
    new NoiseGateTransform(sampleRate: 48000, thresholdDb: -40, ratio: 10, attackMs: 5, releaseMs: 100),
    new VolumeTransform(gain: 1.5),
    new LimiterTransform(sampleRate: 48000, ceilingDb: -0.3, releaseMs: 50));

AudioCutter.Convert(sourcePath, destPath, pipeline);
```

Transforms run in the order given; each receives the previous one's output. **A pipeline instance carries cross-block state and is meant for exactly one `Convert`/`Cut`/`Mix` call -- build a fresh `PcmTransformPipeline` per call, never reuse one across calls.**

```csharp
public interface IPcmTransform
{
    int OutputSampleRate { get; }      // 0 = passthrough
    int OutputChannels { get; }        // 0 = passthrough
    int OutputBitsPerSample { get; }   // 0 = passthrough
    bool CanChangeFrameCount { get; }
    (int[] buffer, int frameCount) Apply(int[] buffer, int frameCount, int channels, int sampleRate, int bitsPerSample);

    // Default interface method -- existing implementers don't need to change. Drains output this
    // transform is still holding back (e.g. a resampler's pending tail); call once, after the last
    // Apply() call for a stream. Most transforms hold no such state and keep the default (no output).
    (int[] buffer, int frameCount) Flush() => (Array.Empty<int>(), 0);
}
```

### The thirteen built-in transforms

```csharp
public sealed class ResamplingTransform : IPcmTransform
{
    public const int DefaultFilterHalfWidth = 32;
    public ResamplingTransform(int sourceRate, int targetRate, int channels, int filterHalfWidth = DefaultFilterHalfWidth);
    public int FilterHalfWidth { get; }
    public void Reset();
}

public sealed class VolumeTransform : IPcmTransform
{
    public VolumeTransform(double gain); // 1.0 = no change, 0.0 = silence
}

public sealed class PeakNormalizationTransform : IPcmTransform
{
    public PeakNormalizationTransform(double targetDb); // e.g. -1.0; must be <= 0
    public void MeasurePeak(int[] buffer, int frameCount, int channels, int bitsPerSample);
    public void MeasurePeak(long maxAbsoluteSample, int bitsPerSample);
    public static long ComputeMaxAbsoluteSample(ReadOnlySpan<int> samples);
}

public sealed class CompressorTransform : IPcmTransform
{
    public CompressorTransform(int sampleRate, double thresholdDb, double ratio, double attackMs, double releaseMs, double makeupGainDb = 0.0);
    public void Reset(); // clear the envelope follower back to silence
}

public sealed class NoiseGateTransform : IPcmTransform
{
    // The mirror image of CompressorTransform: gain reduction below threshold instead of above.
    public NoiseGateTransform(int sampleRate, double thresholdDb, double ratio, double attackMs, double releaseMs);
    public void Reset(); // clear the envelope follower back to silence
}

public sealed class LimiterTransform : IPcmTransform
{
    // Infinite-ratio compression (envelope clamped AT the ceiling) plus a final per-sample hard
    // clip, so the output is GUARANTEED never to exceed the ceiling even during a nonzero attack.
    public LimiterTransform(int sampleRate, double ceilingDb, double releaseMs, double attackMs = 0.0);
    public void Reset(); // clear the envelope follower back to silence
}

public sealed class PanTransform : IPcmTransform
{
    public PanTransform(double pan, PanLaw law = PanLaw.Linear); // pan: -1.0 (full left) .. +1.0 (full right)
    public double Pan { get; }
    public PanLaw Law { get; }
}
public enum PanLaw { Linear, EqualPower }

public sealed class ChannelRemixTransform : IPcmTransform
{
    public ChannelRemixTransform(int inputChannels, int outputChannels, ChannelRemixMode mixMode = ChannelRemixMode.Auto);
}
public enum ChannelRemixMode { Auto, PassThrough, Downmix, UpMix }

public sealed class BitDepthFormatTransform : IPcmTransform
{
    public BitDepthFormatTransform(int fromBits, int toBits); // each 8, 16, 24, or 32
    public static (long Min, long Max) GetNativeRange(int bits);
}

public sealed class FadeTransform : IPcmTransform
{
    public FadeTransform(long totalFrames, long fadeInFrames = 0, long fadeOutFrames = 0, FadeCurve curve = FadeCurve.Linear);
    public void Reset();
}
public enum FadeCurve { Linear, EqualPower }

public sealed class BiquadTransform : IPcmTransform
{
    public BiquadTransform(BiquadFilterType filterType, int channels, int sampleRate, double frequencyHz, double q = 0.7071067811865476, double gainDb = 0.0);
    public void Reset();
}
public enum BiquadFilterType { LowPass, HighPass, BandPass, Notch, AllPass, PeakingEq, LowShelf, HighShelf }

public sealed class ButterworthTransform : IPcmTransform
{
    public ButterworthTransform(BiquadFilterType filterType, int order, int channels, int sampleRate, double frequencyHz);
    public void Reset();
}

public sealed class FirFilterTransform : IPcmTransform
{
    public FirFilterTransform(int channels, double[] taps);
    public void Reset();
}
```

- **Gain / peak normalization**: `VolumeTransform` is a flat linear multiplier. `PeakNormalizationTransform` measures the peak `|sample|` then applies `gain = targetPeakLinear * bitDepthMax / peak`; dropped into a pipeline without pre-measuring, it self-measures from whatever block `Apply` first sees -- driven by `AudioCutter.Convert`/`Cut`, that's one ~4096-frame decode block, **not the whole file**. For a true whole-file measurement: call `AudioCutter.MeasurePeakAmplitude(sourcePath)` first, then `peakTransform.MeasurePeak(peak, bitsPerSample)` before running the pipeline.
- **Dynamics compression**: `CompressorTransform` is a standard feedforward design (threshold dBFS / ratio / attack / release / makeup gain). Its envelope follower is **stereo-linked** -- one scalar tracking the loudest channel per frame, not independent per-channel envelopes, so a transient in one channel doesn't shift the stereo image. Tracked in linear scale via a one-pole filter with separate attack/release coefficients, converted to dB once per frame for the reduction computation. Channel-count-agnostic (no per-channel state, derives `channels` fresh from each `Apply` call, the same way `FadeTransform` does), but fixes `sampleRate` at construction (the attack/release coefficients depend on it) the same way `BiquadTransform` does.
- **Noise gating**: `NoiseGateTransform` is the mirror image of `CompressorTransform` -- gain reduction below threshold instead of above, via the same stereo-linked envelope follower, one-pole attack/release tracking, and `ratio` convention (`>= 1.0`, where `1.0` is an explicit no-op at every level). Unlike the compressor, true digital silence (`envelopeDb == -Infinity`) is this transform's own common case rather than a boundary condition, so `ratio == 1.0` combined with silence is handled as its own branch rather than falling through the general `(threshold - envelopeDb) * (1 - 1/ratio)` formula -- that combination would otherwise compute `Infinity * 0`, which is `NaN` under IEEE 754, not 0.
- **Peak limiting**: `LimiterTransform` is an infinite-ratio compressor against a `ceilingDb` -- the same stereo-linked envelope follower as `CompressorTransform`/`NoiseGateTransform`, but once the envelope exceeds the ceiling the gain applied brings it exactly down to the ceiling, not some ratio-scaled fraction of the way there. It then also applies a final per-sample hard clip to the ceiling, which is what makes this a true peak limiter rather than just "`CompressorTransform` with a very high ratio": a nonzero attack time lets a fast transient slip past the smoothed envelope follower before gain reduction has caught up, so the envelope-derived gain alone can only reduce toward the ceiling, not guarantee it. `attackMs` defaults to `0` (instant), the classic brick-wall-limiter default.
- **Pan/balance**: `PanTransform` scales left/right gain independently from a single `pan` value. Stereo (2-channel) input only -- throws `ArgumentException` for any other channel count. `PanLaw.Linear` is balance-style (only the opposite channel attenuates; no volume dip at center). `PanLaw.EqualPower` is constant-power (`left^2 + right^2 == 1` everywhere, including a -3dB-per-channel center) -- how a true pan pot behaves in most DAWs.
- **Channel remix**: `ChannelRemixTransform` handles mono<->stereo and general N<->M (equal-weight downmix, cyclic upmix).
- **Bit-depth / float conversion**: `BitDepthFormatTransform` rescales between the native ranges of 8/16/24/32-bit samples -- this codebase has no separate "normalized" scale; every bit depth is signed and sign-extended to its own native range (e.g. 8-bit is -128..127).
- **Fades**: `FadeTransform` applies a fade-in/out (linear or equal-power) over a fixed total frame count, tracked across blocks the same way `ResamplingTransform` tracks its own state. Reachable directly, or via `CutOptions.FadeInSeconds`/`FadeOutSeconds`/`FadeCurve` on a `Cut` call.
- **Parametric EQ**: `BiquadTransform` is a single second-order IIR filter section using the RBJ Audio EQ Cookbook formulas (Direct Form II Transposed, two state values per channel) -- low/high pass, band pass, notch, all pass, peaking EQ, low/high shelf. `ButterworthTransform` cascades `order / 2` `BiquadTransform` stages sharing one cutoff, each at a different Q from the standard Butterworth pole-pair formula, for a steeper, maximally-flat-passband low/high pass than one biquad section alone.
- **General FIR convolution**: `FirFilterTransform` applies a caller-supplied tap array identically to every channel (parity with ffmpeg's `afir`/general-FIR filters) -- no filter-design code of its own, since accepting arbitrary taps is the whole point. Keeps each channel's last `taps.Length - 1` samples as history across blocks.
- **Mixing/concatenation**: `AudioCutter.Mix` (2+ same-format sources, per-input gain, silence-padded to the longest, decodes every input fully into memory concurrently -- clip-length material, not multi-hour streams) and `AudioCutter.Concatenate` (2+ same-format sources, fully streaming for non-WAV destinations) are separate, non-transform capabilities reachable through the same opt-in API, not `IPcmTransform` implementations.

### Important limits an LLM should surface when recommending this

- A `PcmTransformPipeline` instance carries cross-block state (resampler history, fade frame position, measured peak gain, compressor/gate/limiter envelope, biquad/Butterworth/FIR filter history) -- build a fresh instance per `Convert`/`Cut`/`Mix` call, never reuse one across calls.
- Any transform implementing `IPcmTransform.Flush` (currently only `ResamplingTransform`) holds output back until it has enough lookahead, and needs `pipeline.Flush(channels, sampleRate, bitsPerSample)` called once after the last block to drain its tail. `AudioCutter.Convert(pipeline)`/`Cut(options)` call this automatically; only code driving `PcmTransformPipeline` directly needs to call it itself.
- `Mix`/`Concatenate` require every source to share channels/sample rate/bit depth (mismatches throw `NotSupportedException`).
- `ResamplingTransform` is a Kaiser-windowed-sinc polyphase filter (anti-aliasing on downsample, band-limited reconstruction on upsample), not linear interpolation. It tracks a cumulative `floor(sourceFrames * ratio)` target so total output frame count is exact regardless of block splits; downsampling scales the filter's half-width up to preserve anti-aliasing quality, capped at 256 taps for extreme ratios.
- Float PCM: the pipeline itself is `int[]`-only; `FloatSampleConverter`/`AudioCutter.ReadWavAsFloat`/`WriteWavFromFloat` convert at the application boundary. A float WAV *source* always decodes transparently into int PCM. For a float WAV *destination*, pass `WavSampleFormat.Float32` to `Convert`/`Cut`(`CutOptions.DestinationWavFormat`)/`Mix`/`Concatenate` -- it requires the destination's bit depth to already be 32-bit and throws `NotSupportedException` against a non-WAV destination. NaN samples convert to silence (0); Infinity clamps to +/-1.0.

```csharp
public sealed class CutOptions
{
    public PcmTransformPipeline? Pipeline { get; init; }
    public double FadeInSeconds { get; init; }
    public double FadeOutSeconds { get; init; }
    public FadeCurve FadeCurve { get; init; } = FadeCurve.Linear;
    public WavSampleFormat DestinationWavFormat { get; init; } = WavSampleFormat.Integer;
    public AiffSampleFormat DestinationAiffFormat { get; init; } = AiffSampleFormat.Integer;
    public AuSampleFormat DestinationAuFormat { get; init; } = AuSampleFormat.Integer;
}

public readonly record struct MixInput(string FilePath, double Gain = 1.0);

public enum WavSampleFormat { Integer, Float32, MuLaw, ALaw, ImaAdpcm, MsAdpcm, YamahaAdpcm }
public enum AiffSampleFormat { Integer, LittleEndianInteger, Float32, Float64, MuLaw, ALaw }
public enum AuSampleFormat { Integer, Float32, Float64, MuLaw, ALaw }
```

## Codec Reference

Every codec's `Decode` method takes an `AudioBlockDecodedCallback` (`EggEncoder.Codecs` namespace) instead of a generic `Action<>` -- `ReadOnlySpan<int>` can't be used as a generic type argument on `net8.0`, so this is a plain delegate:

```csharp
public delegate void AudioBlockDecodedCallback(ReadOnlySpan<int> block, int channels, int sampleRate, int bitsPerSample, long totalSamplesPerChannel);
```

`block` is interleaved samples for whatever chunk the decoder just produced. Accumulate it yourself (into a `List<int>`, a `WaveformCalculator`, an internal `IAudioSink` implementation) as needed -- this keeps memory bounded for large files and lets `NativeEncoder`/`AudioCutter` pipe decode output directly into an encoder session without buffering the whole track.

### AAC — `EggEncoder.Codecs.Aac`

```csharp
public static class AacDecoder
{
    public static AacStreamInfo Decode(string aacFilePath, AudioBlockDecodedCallback onBlockDecoded);
}

public static class AacEncoder
{
    public static void Encode(string destFilePath, short[] samples, int channels, int sampleRate);
    // throws NotSupportedException for channels != 1 or unsupported sample rates
}

public sealed class AacEncoderSession : IDisposable
{
    public static AacEncoderSession OpenSession(string destFilePath, int channels, int sampleRate);
    public void WriteInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int frameCount);
}
```

### FLAC — `EggEncoder.Codecs.Flac`

```csharp
public static class FlacDecoder
{
    public static FlacStreamInfo Decode(string flacFilePath, AudioBlockDecodedCallback onBlockDecoded);
}

public static class FlacEncoder
{
    public const uint DefaultCompressionLevel = 5;
    public static void Encode(string sourceWavFilePath, string destFlacFilePath, uint compressionLevel = DefaultCompressionLevel);
}

public sealed class FlacEncoderSession : IDisposable
{
    public static FlacEncoderSession OpenSession(string destFlacFilePath, int channels, int bitsPerSample, int sampleRate, uint compressionLevel = FlacEncoder.DefaultCompressionLevel);
    public void WriteInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int frameCount);
}
```

Both wrap native `libFLAC` P/Invoke bindings (`EggEncoder.Native.FlacNative`).

### MP3 — `EggEncoder.Codecs.Mp3`

```csharp
public static class Mp3Decoder // backed by the NLayer managed decoder -- no native call
{
    public static Mp3StreamInfo Decode(string mp3FilePath, AudioBlockDecodedCallback onBlockDecoded);
}

public static class Mp3Encoder // native libmp3lame P/Invoke
{
    public const int DefaultBitRateKbps = 320;
    public static void Encode(string sourceWavFilePath, string destMp3FilePath, int bitRateKbps = DefaultBitRateKbps);
}

public sealed class Mp3EncoderSession : IDisposable
{
    public static Mp3EncoderSession OpenSession(string destMp3FilePath, int channels, int sampleRate, int bitsPerSample, int bitRateKbps = Mp3Encoder.DefaultBitRateKbps);
    public void WriteInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int frameCount);
}

public static class Mp3Probe // manual MPEG frame-header parsing (Xing/Info/VBRI-aware), no native call
{
    public static Mp3ProbeResult Probe(string mp3FilePath);
    // Mp3ProbeResult: DurationInSeconds, SampleRate, Channels, BitRate, IsVariableBitRate
}
```

### WAV — `EggEncoder.Codecs.Wav`

```csharp
public sealed class WavReader : IDisposable
{
    public static WavReader Open(string filePath);
    public int Channels { get; }
    public int SampleRate { get; }
    public int BitsPerSample { get; }
    public long TotalSamples { get; }
    public bool IsFloatFormat { get; }
    public bool IsALaw { get; }
    public bool IsMuLaw { get; }
    public bool IsImaAdpcm { get; }
    public bool IsMsAdpcm { get; }
    public bool IsYamahaAdpcm { get; }
    public int ReadInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int maxSamplesPerChannel);
}

public sealed class WavWriter : IDisposable
{
    public static WavWriter Create(string destFilePath, int channels, int sampleRate, int bitsPerSample, long totalFrames, WavSampleFormat sampleFormat = WavSampleFormat.Integer);
    public void WriteInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int frameCount);
    public void Finish(); // flushes/pads a pending ADPCM block or trailing Yamaha ADPCM nibble
}
```

See "WAV's own format-tag variants" above for the full ADPCM/G.711 story. Every other codec's `Convert`/`Cut` path reads from or writes to WAV as the common interchange format.

### WMA — `EggEncoder.Codecs.Wma`

```csharp
public static class WmaDecoder
{
    public static WmaStreamInfo Decode(string wmaFilePath, AudioBlockDecodedCallback onBlockDecoded);
    // throws NotSupportedException for mid/side-coded stereo or channel counts other than 1/2
}

public static class WmaEncoder
{
    public static void Encode(string destFilePath, IReadOnlyList<short> interleavedSamples, int channels, int sampleRate);
    // mono or stereo only; always writes independently-coded channels (no mid/side stereo)
}

public sealed class WmaEncoderSession : IDisposable
{
    public static WmaEncoderSession OpenSession(string destFilePath, int channels, int sampleRate);
    public void WriteInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int frameCount);
}
```

Container parsing/writing via the internal `AsfContainerReader`/`AsfContainerWriter`. Mono or independently-coded stereo only -- genuine mid/side-coded stereo WMA files (the real-world default for most third-party encoders, including ffmpeg's) throw `NotSupportedException` on decode; `WmaEncoder` never produces mid/side output, so round-tripping through this library's own encoder/decoder always works.

### AIFF / AIFC — `EggEncoder.Codecs.Aiff`

```csharp
public sealed class AiffReader : IDisposable
{
    public static AiffReader Open(string filePath);
    public int Channels { get; }
    public int SampleRate { get; }
    public int BitsPerSample { get; }
    public long TotalSamples { get; }
    public bool IsFloatFormat { get; }
    public bool IsFloat32 { get; }
    public bool IsFloat64 { get; }
    public bool IsALaw { get; }
    public bool IsMuLaw { get; }
    public bool IsLittleEndian { get; }
    public int ReadInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int maxSamplesPerChannel);
}

public sealed class AiffWriter : IDisposable
{
    public static AiffWriter Create(string filePath, int channels, int sampleRate, int bitsPerSample, long totalFrames);
    public static AiffWriter Create(string filePath, int channels, int sampleRate, int bitsPerSample, long totalFrames, AiffSampleFormat sampleFormat);
    public void WriteInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int frameCount);
}
```

Plain AIFF (FORM/AIFF, 8/16/24/32-bit signed integer PCM -- 8-bit is signed, unlike WAV's unsigned convention) both read and write under `AiffSampleFormat.Integer`, the default, under the `.aiff`/`.aif` extensions. `AiffReader` additionally reads AIFC (FORM/AIFC) under the same extensions plus `.aifc`, with no separate dispatch beyond that extension list -- just an extra `compressionType` field it understands in COMM. Every other `AiffSampleFormat` value writes AIFC instead: `LittleEndianInteger` ('sowt'), `Float32`/`Float64` ('fl32'/'fl64', big-endian IEEE float, both reporting `BitsPerSample` 32 since this project's `int[]` model has no 64-bit representation), and `MuLaw`/`ALaw` ('ulaw'/'alaw', G.711, via the same `G711Codec` the WAV side uses). AIFC's `ima4` (QuickTime IMA4 ADPCM) compressionType is also decoded (decode only -- `AiffWriter` never writes it) -- a materially different bitstream from WAV's own IMA ADPCM (no verbatim first sample per block; stereo stores each channel's own complete 34-byte sub-block consecutively rather than nibble-interleaving), though the underlying per-nibble math is identical and reused directly from `Wav.ImaAdpcmDecoder`. Any other, genuinely unsupported compressionType (e.g. `MAC3`/MACE) throws `NotSupportedException` naming it specifically.

### AU — `EggEncoder.Codecs.Au`

```csharp
public sealed class AuReader : IDisposable
{
    public static AuReader Open(string filePath);
    public int Channels { get; }
    public int SampleRate { get; }
    public int BitsPerSample { get; }
    public long TotalSamples { get; }
    public bool IsFloatFormat { get; }
    public bool IsFloat32 { get; }
    public bool IsFloat64 { get; }
    public bool IsALaw { get; }
    public bool IsMuLaw { get; }
    public int ReadInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int maxSamplesPerChannel);
}

public sealed class AuWriter : IDisposable
{
    public static AuWriter Create(string filePath, int channels, int sampleRate, int bitsPerSample, long totalFrames);
    public static AuWriter Create(string filePath, int channels, int sampleRate, int bitsPerSample, long totalFrames, AuSampleFormat sampleFormat);
    public void WriteInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int frameCount);
}
```

Sun/NeXT AU (magic `.snd`, mime `audio/basic`) -- no chunk structure at all: one fixed 24-byte header, optionally followed by an annotation string (never parsed), then raw big-endian samples with no byte-alignment padding requirement. `AuSampleFormat.Integer` (the default) covers 8/16/24/32-bit signed integer PCM -- AU's 8-bit is signed, the same convention AIFF uses. `Float32`/`Float64` are big-endian IEEE float (both report `BitsPerSample` 32). `MuLaw`/`ALaw` are G.711, via the same `G711Codec` the WAV/AIFF sides use. Every other defined AU encoding (G.721/G.722/G.723 ADPCM, fragmented samples) is real but obscure enough in practice that it's out of scope, the same way AIFC's `MAC3`/`MAC6` (MACE) are -- throws `NotSupportedException` naming the unrecognized encoding value. AU also has its own "unknown data size" sentinel a real streaming file can use; `AuReader` reads until end-of-file for it, though `AuWriter` never writes it (it always knows its exact `totalFrames` up front, like `WavWriter`/`AiffWriter`).

### ALAC — `EggEncoder.Codecs.Alac`

```csharp
public static class AlacDecoder
{
    public static AlacStreamInfo Decode(string filePath, AudioBlockDecodedCallback onBlockDecoded);
}

public static class AlacEncoder
{
    public static void Encode(string sourceWavFilePath, string destAlacFilePath);
}

public sealed class AlacEncoderSession : IDisposable
{
    public static AlacEncoderSession OpenSession(string destFilePath, int channels, int sampleRate, int bitsPerSample);
    public void WriteInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int frameCount);
}
```

Apple Lossless, in a CAF container (`.caf`). Mono and stereo, 16-bit or 24-bit integer PCM only -- throws `NotSupportedException` for any other channel count or bit depth (20-bit and 32-bit are out of scope, matching ffmpeg's own ALAC encoder). For stereo, the encoder tries a fixed mid/side mix first (the classic 0.5-weight split), falling back to independent channels and then to a verbatim (uncompressed) frame only if the previous option's residuals would overflow the Rice coder's escape code.

### TTA — `EggEncoder.Codecs.Tta`

```csharp
public static class TtaDecoder
{
    public static TtaStreamInfo Decode(string filePath, AudioBlockDecodedCallback onBlockDecoded);
}

public static class TtaEncoder
{
    public static void Encode(string sourceWavFilePath, string destTtaFilePath);
}

public sealed class TtaEncoderSession : IDisposable
{
    public static TtaEncoderSession OpenSession(string destFilePath, int channels, int sampleRate, int bitsPerSample);
    public void WriteInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int frameCount);
}
```

True Audio, a lossless codec (`.tta`). Mono and stereo, 16-bit integer PCM only -- throws `NotSupportedException` for any other channel count or bit depth. Unlike ALAC, TTA's stereo decorrelation is unconditional (no bitstream flag, no fallback), and its Rice/unary residual coder has no escape code -- the unary code is fully unbounded, so there's no verbatim/overflow fallback path.

### WavPack — `EggEncoder.Codecs.WavPack`

```csharp
public static class WavPackDecoder
{
    public static WavPackStreamInfo Decode(string filePath, AudioBlockDecodedCallback onBlockDecoded);
}

public static class WavPackEncoder
{
    public static void Encode(string sourceWavFilePath, string destWvFilePath);
}

public sealed class WavPackEncoderSession : IDisposable
{
    public static WavPackEncoderSession OpenSession(string destFilePath, int channels, int bitsPerSample, int sampleRate, long totalSamples);
    public void WriteInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int frameCount);
}
```

Lossless, in its own `.wv` container. Mono and stereo, 16-bit or 24-bit integer PCM only (WavPack's own lossy/hybrid and floating-point modes are rejected) -- throws `NotSupportedException` otherwise. Unlike every other codec here, WavPack delegates to a native binary (`wavpackdll.dll`, the official WavPack project's own prebuilt library) rather than a pure-managed implementation, since no pure-managed WavPack decoder/encoder exists on NuGet. `OpenSession` requires an exact, positive `totalSamples` up front (like `WavWriter`/`AiffWriter`) -- WavPack genuinely cannot represent an empty/zero-sample stream at all (confirmed from its own reference CLI, which refuses to encode one), so a zero or negative total throws `NotSupportedException` rather than producing a file that would only turn out to be unreadable later.

### Opus — `EggEncoder.Codecs.Opus`

```csharp
public static class OpusDecoder
{
    public static OpusStreamInfo Decode(string filePath, AudioBlockDecodedCallback onBlockDecoded);
}

public static class OpusEncoder
{
    public static void Encode(string sourceWavFilePath, string destOpusFilePath);
}

public sealed class OpusEncoderSession : IDisposable
{
    public static OpusEncoderSession OpenSession(string destFilePath, int channels, int sampleRate, int bitsPerSample);
    public void WriteInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int frameCount);
}
```

Lossy, in a from-scratch OggOpus container (`.opus`). Mono and stereo, 16-bit integer PCM, and fixed at 48kHz (Opus's native/highest internal rate) regardless of the source's own rate -- encoding at any other rate throws `NotSupportedException`; resample first with `ResamplingTransform`. The actual Opus codec (SILK+CELT) is delegated to Concentus, a pure managed C# port (NuGet package, the same "lean on an established pure-managed implementation" precedent `NLayer` sets for MP3 decode); EggEncoder implements the OggOpus container itself (page framing, CRC-32, the mandatory `OpusHead`/`OpusTags` packets) from scratch. Channel mapping family 0 only.

### Vorbis — `EggEncoder.Codecs.Vorbis`

```csharp
public static class VorbisDecoder
{
    public static VorbisStreamInfo Decode(string filePath, AudioBlockDecodedCallback onBlockDecoded);
}

public static class VorbisEncoder
{
    public const float DefaultQuality = 0.5f;
    public static void Encode(string sourceWavFilePath, string destOggFilePath, float quality = DefaultQuality);
}

public sealed class VorbisEncoderSession : IDisposable
{
    public static VorbisEncoderSession OpenSession(string destFilePath, int channels, int sampleRate, int bitsPerSample, float quality = DefaultQuality);
    public void WriteInterleavedSamples(int[] buffer, int frameCount);
}
```

Lossy, in an Ogg container (`.ogg`). Mono and stereo, 16-bit integer PCM -- throws `NotSupportedException` otherwise; unlike Opus, any positive sample rate is accepted, no fixed-rate resampling requirement. The codec and the Ogg container are both delegated to third-party pure managed NuGet packages -- NVorbis for decode, OggVorbisEncoder for encode -- each with its own independent Ogg object model (EggEncoder's own `Codecs/Opus/OggPageReader`/`OggPageWriter` aren't involved here). Vorbis has no `pre_skip`-equivalent field the way Opus does, so there's no way to tell a decoder exactly how many samples of the encoder's own fixed MDCT lookahead to trim off the front -- finding the true alignment (e.g. via cross-correlation) is left to the caller if exact alignment matters.

### MOV/MP4 — `EggEncoder.Codecs.Mov`

```csharp
public static class MovProbe
{
    public static MovProbeResult Probe(string filePath); // walks the ISO base media atom tree directly
}

public class MovProbeResult
{
    public int DurationInSeconds { get; init; }
    public double DurationSeconds { get; init; }
    public int? Width { get; init; }
    public int? Height { get; init; }
    public string? CodecFourCc { get; init; }
}

public static class MovDecoder
{
    public static MovStreamInfo Decode(string filePath, AudioBlockDecodedCallback onBlockDecoded);
    // finds the 'soun' track, reads its esds AudioSpecificConfig + sample table, and decodes each
    // sample through the same AacFrameDecoder engine AacDecoder uses -- MP4 stores raw AAC access
    // units with no ADTS framing, so there's no header to parse per sample. Mono AAC-LC only; throws
    // InvalidDataException if there's no audio track, NotSupportedException for a non-AAC codec,
    // stereo, or any other MPEG-4 audio object type.
}
```

`MovProbe` is metadata-only (no native dependency, no decode). `MovDecoder` decodes a mono AAC-LC audio track when present; video frames are never decoded.

## AudioCutter — `EggEncoder.Codecs`

Format-dispatching convert/cut/mix/concatenate used internally by `NativeEncoder`; also usable directly:

```csharp
public static class AudioCutter
{
    public static void Convert(string sourceFilePath, string destFilePath);
    public static bool Cut(string sourceFilePath, string destFilePath, int startInSeconds, int endInSeconds);

    // Pipeline-aware overloads: run every decoded block through a PcmTransformPipeline first.
    public static void Convert(string sourceFilePath, string destFilePath, PcmTransformPipeline pipeline);
    public static bool Cut(string sourceFilePath, string destFilePath, int startInSeconds, int endInSeconds, CutOptions options);

    // WavSampleFormat/AiffSampleFormat/AuSampleFormat overloads select a destination's on-disk
    // encoding (each defaults to Integer, matching every overload above); ignored for a destination
    // of a different family.
    public static void Convert(string sourceFilePath, string destFilePath, WavSampleFormat destinationWavFormat);
    public static void Convert(string sourceFilePath, string destFilePath, PcmTransformPipeline pipeline, WavSampleFormat destinationWavFormat);
    public static void Convert(string sourceFilePath, string destFilePath, AiffSampleFormat destinationAiffFormat);
    public static void Convert(string sourceFilePath, string destFilePath, PcmTransformPipeline pipeline, AiffSampleFormat destinationAiffFormat);
    public static void Convert(string sourceFilePath, string destFilePath, AuSampleFormat destinationAuFormat);
    public static void Convert(string sourceFilePath, string destFilePath, PcmTransformPipeline pipeline, AuSampleFormat destinationAuFormat);

    // Mixes 2+ same-format sources with per-input gain; decodes every input fully into memory, concurrently.
    public static void Mix(IReadOnlyList<MixInput> inputs, string destFilePath);
    public static void Mix(IReadOnlyList<MixInput> inputs, string destFilePath, WavSampleFormat destinationWavFormat);

    // Concatenates 2+ same-format sources, in order. Fully streaming for non-WAV destinations.
    public static void Concatenate(IReadOnlyList<string> sourceFilePaths, string destFilePath);
    public static void Concatenate(IReadOnlyList<string> sourceFilePaths, string destFilePath, WavSampleFormat destinationWavFormat);

    // Decodes sourceFilePath fully to find its peak absolute sample value, for a true whole-file
    // PeakNormalizationTransform.MeasurePeak(long, int) measurement.
    public static (long Peak, int BitsPerSample) MeasurePeakAmplitude(string sourceFilePath);

    // Convenience float[] entry points.
    public static (float[] Samples, int Channels, int SampleRate) ReadWavAsFloat(string sourceFilePath);
    public static void WriteWavFromFloat(string destFilePath, ReadOnlySpan<float> interleavedSamples, int channels, int sampleRate);
}
```

`Cut` decodes any supported source and writes any supported destination extension -- source and destination don't need to match, so it can transcode while it trims. Returns `false` (and writes no file) if the requested range is entirely outside the source's duration.

## Waveform Generation — `EggEncoder.Waveform`

```csharp
public sealed class WaveformCalculator
{
    public const int DefaultWindowCount = 200;

    public WaveformCalculator(long totalSamplesPerChannel, int channels, int bitsPerSample, int windowCount = DefaultWindowCount);
    public void AddBlock(ReadOnlySpan<int> interleavedSamples); // call repeatedly across decode callbacks
    public List<double> GetNormalizedWindows(); // each value in [0, 1]
    public double GetNormalizedPeakAmplitude(); // loudest absolute sample seen so far, in [0, 1] -- no flush step needed
    public double GetNormalizedRmsLevel();      // root-mean-square across every sample seen so far, in [0, 1]
}
```

Example, decoding a WAV file directly instead of via `IMediaEncoder.Probe`:

```csharp
using var wavReader = WavReader.Open("track.wav");
var calculator = new WaveformCalculator(wavReader.TotalSamples, wavReader.Channels, wavReader.BitsPerSample);

var buffer = new int[4096 * wavReader.Channels];
int framesRead;
while ((framesRead = wavReader.ReadInterleavedSamples(buffer, 4096)) > 0)
{
    calculator.AddBlock(new ReadOnlySpan<int>(buffer, 0, framesRead * wavReader.Channels));
}

List<double> windows = calculator.GetNormalizedWindows();
double peak = calculator.GetNormalizedPeakAmplitude();
double rms = calculator.GetNormalizedRmsLevel();
```

`WaveformCalculator` streams -- call `AddBlock` as many times as you like across however many decode callbacks the codec produces; it does not need the full signal in memory at once. `GetNormalizedPeakAmplitude`/`GetNormalizedRmsLevel` need no flushing step the way `GetNormalizedWindows` does (its own trailing partial window) -- both are fully up to date after every `AddBlock` call, and back `ProbeResult.PeakAmplitude`/`RmsLevel` the same way `GetNormalizedWindows` backs `ProbeResult.Waveform`.

## Constraints and Gotchas

- **Native-binary-backed codecs (MP3, FLAC, WavPack) are Windows x64 only.** The pure-managed codecs (AAC, AIFF/AIFC, ALAC, AU, Opus, TTA, Vorbis, WAV incl. all its ADPCM/G.711 variants, WMA) have no such restriction in principle, but this library ships and is CI-tested as a Windows x64 package overall.
- **WAV's three ADPCM variants and G.711** are genuinely different algorithms despite the shared 4-bit (ADPCM) or 8-bit (G.711) coded width -- see "WAV's own format-tag variants" above.
- **`AudioCutter.Cut`/`Convert` can transcode while they trim/convert.** Source and destination extensions no longer need to match.
- **AAC encoding is mono-only** and restricted to a fixed set of MPEG-4 sample rates (see `AacTables.SampleRates`); other combinations throw `NotSupportedException`.
- **WMA supports mono and independently-coded stereo only.** Genuine mid/side-coded stereo WMA files throw `NotSupportedException` on decode; `WmaEncoder` never produces mid/side output.
- **AIFC's `ima4` (QuickTime IMA4 ADPCM) is decode-only.** `AiffWriter` never writes it.
- **ALAC/TTA/WavPack/Opus/Vorbis are each scoped to mono/stereo** and their own specific bit-depth/sample-rate constraints (see each codec's own section above) -- all throw `NotSupportedException` outside that scope, rather than silently producing something subtly wrong.
- **`PcmTransformPipeline` instances carry cross-block state** -- build a fresh one per `Convert`/`Cut`/`Mix` call (see "PCM Transform Pipeline" above for the full list of stateful transforms and the `Flush()` contract).
- **`PanTransform` requires stereo (2-channel) input** -- throws `ArgumentException` for mono or any other channel count.
- **`NoiseGateTransform` with `ratio == 1.0` is an explicit no-op at every level, including true digital silence** -- guarded so it never hits an `Infinity * 0` intermediate (which would otherwise be `NaN` under IEEE 754, not 0).
- **`LimiterTransform` is the one transform here that makes an exact guarantee rather than a statistical reduction** -- "never exceeds the ceiling" comes specifically from its final per-sample hard clip, not from the envelope-derived gain alone, which a nonzero attack time can let a transient briefly slip past.
- **`Mix` decodes every input fully into memory, concurrently** -- clip-length material, not multi-hour streams.

Opus (via Concentus), Vorbis decode (via NVorbis), and Vorbis encode (via OggVorbisEncoder) are pure managed, permissively-licensed NuGet dependencies, not bundled native binaries.
